p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Education in early childhood profoundly shapes cognitive, social, and emotional development. Modern pedagogical approaches emphasize inquiry-based learning, critical thinking, and creativity rather than rote memorization. Exposure to diverse experiences, problem-solving tasks, and collaborative activities enhances adaptability and lifelong learning skills. However, disparities in access, quality of teaching, and socio-economic factors continue to hinder equitable development. Technology integration, including digital learning tools, offers opportunities for personalized education but can also exacerbate distraction and dependency if mismanaged. Parental involvement, teacher training, and culturally relevant curricula significantly influence outcomes. Research indicates that early interventions in literacy, numeracy, and socio-emotional skills have long-term benefits, impacting academic performance and personal growth. Consequently, a holistic approach combining pedagogy, infrastructure, technology, and social support is essential to nurture well-rounded learners.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Time travel, a concept long confined to theoretical physics and science fiction, raises profound questions about causality, determinism, and the nature of temporal reality. Theoretical frameworks such as Einstein’s general relativity allow for hypothetical scenarios involving wormholes, closed timelike curves, and relativistic time dilation. Philosophical debates interrogate the paradoxes of altering past events, including the famous “grandfather paradox,” which challenges logical consistency. While no experimental evidence currently supports backward time travel, forward progression is observable through relativistic effects on high-velocity objects. Advancements in quantum mechanics, including superposition and entanglement, suggest potential mechanisms that might influence temporal perception, though practical application remains speculative. Beyond physics, time travel stimulates ethical, psychological, and narrative exploration, influencing literature, cinema, and popular imagination. Consequently, time travel occupies an intersection of scientific inquiry, philosophical reasoning, and cultural fascination, demonstrating humanity’s enduring curiosity about temporal boundaries.

The headquarters of the International Court of Justice is at:

questions.q: Three cyclists X, Y and Z start together from the same point on a 480 m circular track. X and Y go clockwise at 4 and 6 m/s; Z goes anticlockwise at 8 m/s. When will all three first meet again at the starting point?
questions.why: Lap times 120, 80 and 60 s; LCM = 240 s. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The ratio of students ranked above Kavya to those below her is 2 : 3. The student exactly midway between Rank 1 and Kavya holds Rank 6. What is Kavya's rank from the bottom?
questions.why: (1 + k)/2 = 6 gives k = 11. 10 above, so 15 below: 16th from the bottom. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The Banker's Gain on a bill due 2 years hence is ₹400. The Banker's Discount on the same bill for 4 years at the same rate is ₹3,200. Find the face value.
questions.why: BD for 2 years = 1600, TD = 1600 − 400 = 1200. FV = BD × TD ÷ BG = 4800. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The ratio of the speeds of two trains is 7 : 8. If the second train covers 400 km in 4 hours, find the speed of the first.
questions.why: Second = 100 km/h; first = 7/8 × 100 = 87.5. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: If a non-leap year has 53 Sundays and 53 Mondays, which must be true about the next year?
opts: It will be a leap year starting on a Tuesday
It will have 53 Mondays and 53 Tuesdays
No such non-leap year can exist
questions.why: A 365-day year has only one day occurring 53 times. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: 1 January 2007 was a Monday. What day was 1 January 2008?
questions.why: 2007 is not a leap year: one odd day. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: 8 February 2005 was a Tuesday. What day was 8 February 2004?
questions.why: The span includes 29 Feb 2004: 366 days, two odd days back. GPSC CBRT, Jul 2024.
Differences 402, 474, 552, 636 rise by 72, 78, 84; next +90 gives 726. GPSC CBRT, Jul 2024.

questions.q: Destructive ulceration, bone pains worse at night and a tendency to deformity are features of which miasm?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Syphilis: destruction and ulceration, night aggravation.

questions.q: The ideal prover, according to Hahnemann, is:
opts: healthy, trustworthy and observant of his own sensations
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Provings are done on healthy human beings (§126–127).

questions.q: The 'law of minimum' (minimum dose) is justified because the sick organism is:
opts: highly sensitive to the similar remedy
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Disease raises susceptibility to the similar stimulus.

questions.q: Ailments from disappointed love or grief, with weeping alone, aversion to sympathy and a craving for salt, need:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum mur: silent grief.

questions.q: Delayed, scanty menses, with a mild, weeping disposition, thirstlessness and craving for open air, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Pulsatilla: changeable, mild, better open air.

questions.q: Restless anxiety with a fear of death, and the patient predicting the time of death, during a sudden acute illness, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Aconite predicts the hour of death.

questions.q: The constitutional remedy of the hydrogenoid constitution (worse from damp) is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Grauvogl's hydrogenoid constitution.

questions.q: The vehicle 'sugar of milk' is preferred over cane sugar for trituration because it is:
opts: hard, gritty and only slightly soluble, which aids grinding
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Its hardness helps subdivide the drug.

questions.q: The 'Homoeopathy Central Council Act' was passed in:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. It set up the Central Council of Homoeopathy (now replaced by the National Commission for Homoeopathy, 2020).

questions.q: W. A. Allen's 'Repertory of Intermittent Fevers' is an example of:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. It deals with one clinical group.

questions.q: The process of matching the patient's symptoms with the materia medica after repertorisation is called:
opts: final selection by consulting the materia medica
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The repertory narrows, the materia medica decides.

questions.q: Which lipoprotein carries cholesterol from the tissues back to the liver (reverse cholesterol transport)?
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. HDL is protective; desirable 40 mg/dL or more (60 or more protective).

questions.q: The main buffer of the extracellular fluid is the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Regulated by lungs and kidneys.

questions.q: Granuloma formation is typically seen in:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Chronic granulomatous inflammation.

questions.q: Leprosy is caused by:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Hansen's bacillus.

questions.q: Polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss in a young person suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. May present with ketoacidosis.

questions.q: Dysmenorrhoea with cramping pains relieved by bending double and pressure suggests homoeopathically:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Mag phos is also better from warmth.

questions.q: Convulsions with the head bent backward (opisthotonos) and violent jerks, especially after a head injury, call for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Cicuta: opisthotonos, ill effects of concussion.

questions.q: Rh incompatibility can cause haemolytic disease of the newborn when:
opts: the mother is Rh-negative and the baby Rh-positive
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Anti-D prophylaxis prevents sensitisation.

questions.q: The two most important danger signs in a child with cough or difficult breathing are fast breathing and:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. IMNCI pneumonia signs.

questions.q: A 'sprain' is an injury to a:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A strain affects muscle or tendon.

questions.q: The commonest cause of preventable blindness in India is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Under the National Programme for Control of Blindness.

questions.q: The specificity of a screening test is its ability to identify correctly:
opts: those who do NOT have the disease
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Sensitivity identifies those with disease.

questions.q: Ascertaining the time of death from the body includes all EXCEPT:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Blood group does not change with time.

questions.q: Euthanasia (passive) in India was permitted with safeguards following the Supreme Court judgment in:
opts: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Also recognised living wills.
